title: Blow Ye the Trumpet, Blow
description: Blow Ye the Trumpet, Blow in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Augustus Montague Toplady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 261 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Jubilee Proclaimed”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blow ye the trum-pet, blow, The glad-ly sol-emn sound; Let all the na-tions know, To earth's re-mo-test bound, The year of ju-bi-lee is come; Re-turn, ye ran-somed sin-ners, home.

lines: The year of jubilee is come;
The year of jubilee is come;
The year of jubilee is come;

licence: Public domain: Augustus Montague Toplady died in 1778.
credits: Words by Augustus Montague Toplady (1740–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
